context.why: The four portal roles now exist and decide what their holders can do. Nothing stops somebody deleting one. The likeliest way a portal loses a role is an administrator tidying up the group list in the administration interface, and the moment a role goes, everyone in it silently stops being able to do their job - no error, no signal, just refusals. This story closes that three ways: the deletion and the rename are refused at the point they are attempted, a portal that is serving in production will not start with a role missing and names the ones it cannot find, and in development the same condition is reported on demand instead of blocking anybody.
spec_sections: User Story 3 - The roles cannot be lost by accident
Requirements / Installation and repair (FR-012 to FR-017)
plan_sections: Phases / Phase 3 - US-3, the roles cannot be lost by accident
prior_decisions: D11 - the production boot refusal MUST stand down for the command that repairs the condition. fairdm.E300 runs in FairDMConfig.ready(), which fires before migrate does any work, and the post_migrate receiver is the only thing that installs the roles. Without the stand-down a production portal upgrading to this version can neither start nor migrate, and nothing inside it can repair that. This was a critical design-review finding; T024 covers the upgrade path explicitly.

Research R4 - E300 is one more check tagged DeployTags.deploy and DeployTags.production_critical with deploy=True, not a new mechanism. It returns no error when the group table is absent or unreadable (ProgrammingError/OperationalError), which is how an unmigrated database is told apart from a portal missing its roles.

Research R6 - a raising pre_delete/pre_save receiver is this codebase's own idiom (see refuse_off_vocabulary_role in contributors/apps.py) and holds for every ORM writer, but it cannot explain itself: in the administration interface it surfaces as a server error. FR-012 and FR-013 both require a message naming the role, so the receivers are the enforcement and a Group administration class is the explanation. The pre_save guard must fire only for an existing row, or PortalRoles.reconcile()'s own get_or_create is refused by the receiver it just installed.
PortalRoles.shipped_names() is the list of protected names. Never hard-code the four names anywhere in this story.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given a shipped role, When something attempts to delete it, Then the deletion is refused and the role and its members survive; When something attempts to rename it, Then the name is unchanged; When a group is created, including by reconcile() itself, Then nothing interferes; and a group the portal created for itself deletes and renames normally.

Given the contributors application's ready(), When it starts, Then pre_delete and pre_save receivers on Group are connected with dispatch_uids, and each raises with a message naming the role and saying FairDM requires it.

Given the administration interface, When an administrator looks at a shipped role, Then no delete action and no delete button is offered for it; When they change its name on the change form and save, Then they get a field error naming the role rather than a server error.
Given the Group administration class registered on CustomAdminSite, When the target is a shipped role, Then has_delete_permission is False and the form refuses a change to name.

Given a migrated database missing two roles, When the check runs, Then it returns one error naming both; with all four present, nothing; with no group table at all, nothing. Given the production baseline and that database, When the portal starts, Then it refuses and names them; in development it starts and `check --deploy` reports them. Given a production database holding data but none of the four roles, When migrate runs, Then it completes - this is the upgrade path of every portal already running and it must not be blocked.

Given fairdm/conf/checks.py, When check_portal_roles_present is registered, Then it carries id fairdm.E300, the deploy and production_critical tags, tolerates an absent or unreadable group table, and stands down for the command that installs the roles.
